title: Moonglade
body: Moonglade is the sacred valley of the druids, a hidden forest ringed by high mountains between Felwood and Winterspring. The only road in runs through the tunnels of Timbermaw Hold. Druids have revered this place since ancient days: the demigod Cenarius once dwelt here, and here Malfurion Stormrage gathered the first druids into the Cenarion Circle. Its wooded hills hide barrow dens where druids sleep while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream, and in the Third War Tyrande Whisperwind fought her way here to wake Malfurion from his. In the years after Hyjal the glade was opened to druids of every race, tauren as well as night elf, under the guardianship of Keeper Remulos, son of Cenarius. The village of Nighthaven stands beside Lake Elune'ara, and its wardens allow no fighting, so Horde and Alliance meet here as guests of the Circle. Yet the peace has limits. The druids of Moonglade and the Arch Druid of Darnassus regard each other with growing mistrust, and Malfurion's spirit has not returned from the Dream.

title: Nighthaven
body: Nighthaven is the village of Moonglade and the seat of the Cenarion Circle, a quiet cluster of night elf halls and moonwells near the shore of Lake Elune'ara. Its welcome extends to every being who respects the authority and command of nature, on one condition: the balance must be kept, and the Moonglade Wardens are trained to end any hostility without question. Loganaar trains druids here and warns the young that one day the Emerald Dream will call them into a long hibernation. Keeper Remulos' majordomo Rabine Saturna receives visitors, the eccentric archivist Umber keeps the Circle's records, and merchants serve those passing through. Only druids may take the Circle's flights to Thunder Bluff and Rut'theran Village.

title: Lake Elune'ara
body: Lake Elune'ara fills the heart of Moonglade, a broad sheet of clear water bearing the name of the moon goddess. Young druids learning the aquatic form dive into its depths for a shrine bauble that crumbles away quickly, then race with it to the Shrine of Remulos, sometimes against other students on the same errand. Its waters have a deeper virtue: Keeper Remulos uses them to dissolve the nightmares clinging to objects touched by the corruption in the Dream, and during one such cleansing the spirit of Malfurion Stormrage appeared to him. Above this lake, too, Remulos once opened a rift into the Dream to draw out the corrupted dragon Eranikus.

title: Shrine of Remulos
body: West of Nighthaven stands the Shrine of Remulos, honoring the keeper who guides the Cenarion Circle in preserving nature and its balance. Remulos keeps watch there, and the warden Tajarri expects every visitor to behave as befits sacred ground. Young druids end their Trial of the Lake here, and in the shrine's presence they join the halves of the Pendant of the Sea Lion. The shrine is among the places in the glade most closely tied to the Emerald Dream, and from here Remulos can send a willing visitor into the Dream itself, warning that nightmares lie in wait. Champions of the war in Icecrown have gone in this way, seeking acorns of restoring power for a stricken crusader.

title: Stormrage Barrow Dens
body: The hills of southeastern Moonglade hold the Stormrage Barrow Dens, sacred chambers where night elf druids sleep while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. They are named for Malfurion Stormrage, who slept within them through the ages, and the Circle still keeps his sleeping body in the glade, for his spirit has not returned. Dreamwardens stand guard. In the southernmost den sleeps Clintar Dreamwalker, and the horrors stalking his chamber are echoes of what he battles within the Dream, a force invading it from outside. Morthis Whisperwing, once of the Druids of the Talon who taught the mysteries of flight, sends his apprentice to wake him, for Clintar's spirit can lead the way to the relics of Aviana.

title: Keeper Remulos
body: Keeper Remulos, son of the demigod Cenarius, keeps Moonglade, the sacred heart of all druidic study. He welcomed the tauren into the Circle; he and Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm trust each other little. His brother Zaetar fell long ago, slain by the centaur he fathered with Princess Theradras, and Remulos thought him lost to arrogance and anger. When a seed grown from Zaetar's remains in Maraudon was brought to him, with word that his brother's spirit lived on there at peace, Remulos took it as proof that Zaetar had been reborn into nature. Of late he speaks of the Emerald Dream with grave unease, fearing for those who gave up their waking lives to save it.

title: Rabine Saturna
body: Rabine Saturna is Keeper Remulos' majordomo, the night elf who welcomes all who come to aid the Circle on behalf of every denizen of the glade. To Horde volunteers he says that the tauren's devotion to the tenets of Cenarius has earned the Horde a welcome here. To the Alliance, knowing the Arch Druid of Darnassus frowned on their coming, he promises safety from any ill-conceived repercussions, for the work serves the greater good. Umber calls him the den mother of their little bear camp. Behind his courtesy lies a private devotion: the memory of Millicent Serene, Milli as he calls her, the naturalist of Eldre'Thalas whose crowning creation is now being twisted into the Felvine.

title: Dendrite Starblaze
body: Dendrite Starblaze is the night elf druid in Nighthaven to whom the young druids of Darnassus and Thunder Bluff alike are sent. He greets every visitor in the Circle's name and asks that the balance be kept. To the young he is guide and examiner at once: he sends them to the Great Bear Spirit, sets the trials of the lake and the sea lion, and answers cries for help from distant villages by sending students to do real work rather than staged tests. When a new druid first stands before him, he traces an unseen gesture in the air, an aura of power settles over him, and he murmurs to Father Cenarius that it has begun.

title: Umber
body: Umber is the Cenarion Circle's archivist in Nighthaven, a human among the night elves of the glade. He can lay hands on anything the Circle has stored away, provided the asker already knows what they are looking for, an arrangement he finds brilliant. Layo Starstrike in Silithus calls him touched but brilliant, a man who has saved tomes in worse shape than anyone thought could be saved. His manners are his own. He will tell a weary traveler frankly that they smell a bit ripe, and he has no love for anything bug-like, which suits him well enough: the horrors of Silithus can stay out there, and he can stay here with the books.

title: Tajarri
body: Tajarri is a night elf warden of Moonglade, posted at the Shrine of Remulos. Guarding the shrine is her duty and her privilege, she says, and she expects visitors to conduct themselves as guests on sacred ground, at least those who would rather not have her scimitar buried in them. She also has a hand in the teaching of young druids. Students who race up from Lake Elune'ara with a crumbling shrine bauble report to her to finish the Trial of the Lake, and she congratulates each one warmly before setting the Trial of the Sea Lion and sending them to ask the people of the glade where the two halves of the pendant may lie.

title: Great Bear Spirit
body: In the northwest of Moonglade dwells the Great Bear Spirit, a wise and noble being the druids say has been part of Azeroth for as long as Azeroth has existed. It speaks without moving its mouth, its voice simply heard, and every druid of the Claw comes to it at the start of the path. It represents the strength that bolsters a young druid, and teaches two lessons. Strength of body is power and swiftness, the bear's great girth hiding a lithe agility and a sharp mind. Strength of heart is the resolve to act from pure intent, the conviction of a mother bear guarding her young. Keeping the balance, it warns, is never mere complacency.

title: Bunthen Plainswind and Silva Fil'naveth
body: Two flight masters stand together in Nighthaven, and they serve druids alone. Silva Fil'naveth, a night elf, offers the Cenarion Circle's flight to Rut'theran Village below Darnassus, while her tauren counterpart Bunthen Plainswind carries druids to Thunder Bluff, and each sends the other's people to their partner. In that small courtesy lies the glade's whole purpose: night elf and tauren side by side in the Circle's service. Anyone else who asks for a ride is told plainly that they are not a druid. Other travelers must make do with the hippogryph master Sindrayl and the wind rider master Faustron, who keep their own posts out in the open glade beyond the village.

title: The Way of the Claw
body: When a young druid is ready to learn the shape of the bear, the trainer, Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus or Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, teaches the spell that carries druids to Moonglade and sends the student to Dendrite Starblaze. The night elf is reminded that all druids are welcome there, whatever the tensions between the Arch Druid and Keeper Remulos; the tauren is told that Remulos watches over every druid who sleeps in the glade. Dendrite sends the student on to the Great Bear Spirit, mentor to every druid, which teaches strength of body and strength of heart and sends them away with its blessing and a warning that their strength will be tested. Dendrite senses the new wisdom and sends them home. The last test lies beyond the glade, at a Moonkin Stone near Auberdine or on the edge of the Barrens by Mulgore, where the spirit Lunaclaw must be faced before the way of the Claw is learned.

title: The Trials of the Lake and the Sea Lion
body: The aquatic form is a blessing that must be earned. Druids who have grown into worthy protectors of nature are sent from Darnassus and Thunder Bluff to Dendrite Starblaze, who sets them two trials. The first tests work in water under pressure: the student dives into Lake Elune'ara for a shrine bauble, which decays rapidly, and must carry it to the Shrine of Remulos before it fails, perhaps racing other druids on the same errand. Using it there honors the shrine, and the warden Tajarri congratulates each one who succeeds. The second tests understanding of the form itself. The Pendant of the Sea Lion must be made whole from two halves, one holding the sea lion's agility in the water, the other its endurance, and the people of the glade hold the clues to where they lie. Joined at the shrine, the pendant teaches that neither trait can stand without the other, and the trainer at home completes the lesson.

title: Lessons Anew
body: Druids can purge poison with a single incantation, a gift of Cenarius not to be taken lightly. Before they learn it, the trainers of Darnassus and Thunder Bluff send their students to Dendrite Starblaze to learn what poison means for those without that power. There are no staged trials here, for real calls for help have reached Moonglade. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong cannot stop a sickness among the deer of Darkshore; the student finds foul water at the Cliffspring Falls and gathers earthroot and lunar fungus from the moonkin caves for a salve. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem faces the same among the gazelles of the northern Barrens, and the water drawn from Dreadmist Peak, where the Burning Blade dwell, proves just as foul; his salve needs earthroot and kodo horn. When ten animals are cured, Dendrite calls them unwitting victims of a greater taint spreading through the land. Some in Darnassus ignore it, he warns, while the tauren prove that balance transcends racial barriers.

title: The Fruit of Fertility
body: Agents of the Cenarion Circle have brought Rabine Saturna troubling news from Eldre'Thalas, the ruin now called Dire Maul. Long ago a night elf naturalist there, Millicent Serene, willed the power of nature into artifacts, and her crowning work was the Fruit of Fertility, a vibrant vine grown from a specially prepared moonwell whose aura of protection and growth made all of Eldre'Thalas flourish. The Circle believed it destroyed in the War of the Ancients. It survived, and the demon Alzzin the Wildshaper is corrupting it into the Felvine. Rabine will not let that corruption run its course, for the world's sake and for Milli's memory. So vile a thing can only be held in a Reliquary of Purity, and Rabine had quietly kept a secret: one lay in the ruins of Southwind Village in Silithus, untouched lest prying rouse the Circle's enemies. Once it is recovered and Alzzin falls, a shard of the Felvine is sealed inside for the Circle to study, and its bearer is welcomed as a hero of the Circle.

title: The Redemption of Eranikus
body: The green shard of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands was held by Eranikus, a dragon of Ysera's flight whom the Old Gods had twisted into a tyrant of the Dream. In the Sunken Temple, Malfurion told the champion seeking it that there was only one way: bring Eranikus into the world. A wisp outside Darnassus carried word to Tyrande and sent the champion to Keeper Remulos. Eranikus could never be pulled from the Dream against his will, Remulos explained, but he wished to come, for he meant to destroy Malfurion's sleeping body. First came fragments of the Nightmare's corruption, taken from dragonkin at the four dream portals. Then, above Lake Elune'ara and well away from Malfurion, Remulos opened the rift. Eranikus demanded Shan'do Stormrage and loosed his nightmare servants on Nighthaven, while its defenders held them off and spared the dragon until Tyrande came. Her prayers drove out the madness, and the redeemed Eranikus returned to the Dream to aid Malfurion, Cenarius and Ysera, leaving the shard behind.

title: Shrouded in Nightmare
body: When four dragons of Ysera's flight came forth from the dream portals, corrupted, those who brought one down found an object engulfed in nightmares that seemed to tie them to the Dream. Only a druid of great power could read it. In Moonglade, Keeper Remulos took it, saying it might explain his recent failures to reach into the Dream, and led its bearer to Lake Elune'ara, whose waters dissolve such nightmares. As the taint washed away, Malfurion Stormrage appeared to his old friend, the message having found its way to him. A new foe fought them in the Dream, Malfurion said, born of an ancient evil: Ysera's noble brood had fallen to the old whisperings, and the Nightmare sought a new host on Azeroth. Cenarius fought at his side, while Illidan brooded on his throne in Outland, sunk in madness. Then Malfurion was drawn back, asking Remulos to tell Tyrande he was safe and would return. His signet ring went to the one who had carried the message.

title: The Journal Under the Chitin
body: Rabine Saturna's call to Horde and Alliance alike leads beyond Tanaris and Un'Goro, to the wasteland of Silithus. Few know, he says, that the night elves once fought a malign and alien power there; it was sealed away, but the Circle suspects that something now works to stir it. He sends volunteers with a letter to Layo Starstrike at Valor's Rest, and in time the work there sends one of them home to Nighthaven with a book-shaped thing pried from a silithid hive and crusted in chitin. Umber the archivist promises to crack its shell and sends the bearer on to the den mother, who must never be kept waiting unless one cares to be doused in honey. Rabine offers the Circle's thanks and expects more secrets from Silithus. Umber keeps his word. The object was indeed a book, a journal in a very ancient dialect of the Darnassian tongue. Its study will take him a long while, but he declares it extremely valuable to the Circle, and the den mother is thrilled.
